title: Lectura en voz alta: plática y fin de semana
titleEn: Read aloud: small talk and the weekend

exercises.text: ¡Qué padre que ya sea viernes! Ojalá no llueva y podamos ir al parque.
exercises.meaningEn: How great that it is already Friday! I hope it does not rain and we can go to the park.

glosses.qué: what; how (qué bueno que = how good that)
glosses.padre: great, cool (Mexican slang: qué padre = how cool)
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.sea: is — present subjunctive of ser, after qué padre que / qué bueno que
glosses.llueva: (it) rains — present subjunctive of llover, after ojalá
glosses.podamos: (we) can — present subjunctive of poder, after ojalá

note.en: Qué padre means how nice in Mexico. It takes the subjunctive with que: que ya sea viernes.
note.es: Qué padre significa qué bueno o qué chido en México. Con que + emoción, el verbo va en subjuntivo.

exercises.text: Platícame cómo te fue en Xochimilco; dicen que, aunque haya mucha gente, el paseo en trajinera vale la pena.
exercises.meaningEn: Tell me how it went in Xochimilco; they say that, even if there are a lot of people, the trajinera ride is worth it.

glosses.platícame: tell me, chat with me — command of platicar + me
glosses.fue: went; was (te fue = it went for you)
glosses.xochimilco: Xochimilco (district of Mexico City; x sounds like s)
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.aunque: although, even if (+ subjunctive when uncertain)
glosses.haya: there is — present subjunctive of haber
glosses.vale: is worth (vale la pena = it is worth it)
glosses.pena: effort, shame (vale la pena = it is worth it)

note.en: Platicar means to chat in Mexico. Say the x in Xochimilco as s: so-chi-MIL-co.
note.es: Platicar es conversar en México. La x de Xochimilco suena como s, y se escribe así por el náhuatl.

exercises.text: Tal vez vayamos a Oaxaca en cuanto tengamos vacaciones, aunque quién sabe si alcancemos boletos baratos.
exercises.meaningEn: Maybe we will go to Oaxaca as soon as we have vacation, though who knows if we will find cheap tickets.

note.en: Tal vez takes the subjunctive when the speaker is unsure.
note.es: Tal vez lleva subjuntivo cuando el hablante no está seguro. Quién sabe si expresa duda.

exercises.text: Si no tuviera que trabajar mañana, me quedaría platicando contigo toda la noche, pero mejor me voy a dormir.
exercises.meaningEn: If I did not have to work tomorrow, I would stay up chatting with you all night, but I had better go to sleep.

glosses.tuviera: (I) had — imperfect subjunctive of tener, after si
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.mejor: better, rather (sería mejor que = it would be better if)
glosses.voy: I go (voy a + infinitive = I am going to)
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)

note.en: Si plus imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional: quedaría. Mejor me voy is a common way to end a talk.
note.es: Si + imperfecto de subjuntivo, y luego el condicional: me quedaría. Mejor me voy es una forma natural de despedirse.

exercises.text: Mi vecino hizo una carne asada el domingo y vinieron tantos amigos que se acabó el carbón.
exercises.meaningEn: My neighbor had a barbecue on Sunday and so many friends came that the charcoal ran out.

glosses.hizo: (he) made, held — preterite of hacer (se me hizo tarde = I ran late)
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.se: himself, itself; (le → se); se acabó = it ran out
glosses.acabó: (it) ran out, ended — preterite of acabarse

note.en: Tantos … que shows a result in the indicative. Se acabó el carbón means the charcoal ran out, and nobody is blamed.
note.es: Tantos … que presenta una consecuencia, en indicativo. Se acabó el carbón: la construcción con se evita nombrar al culpable.

exercises.text: Cuando tengamos tiempo, vamos a recorrer los puestos del mercado y a probar los tacos de barbacoa.
exercises.meaningEn: When we have time, we are going to walk through the market stalls and try the barbacoa tacos.

glosses.tengamos: (we) have — present subjunctive of tener, after aunque / cuando
glosses.vamos: we go (vamos a + infinitive = we are going to)
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)
glosses.barbacoa: barbecued meat, slow-cooked in an underground oven

note.en: Cuando takes the subjunctive for a future event. Trill the rr in recorrer.
note.es: Cuando + subjuntivo para el futuro. Cuida la rr de recorrer: la lengua vibra varias veces.

exercises.text: No creo que el partido empiece a tiempo, así que mejor llegamos un poco más tarde.
exercises.meaningEn: I do not think the game will start on time, so we had better arrive a little later.

exercises.text: Anímate a venir a la fiesta; no tienes que traer nada, solo ganas de pasarla bien y de convivir.
exercises.meaningEn: Come on, join the party; you do not have to bring anything, just the wish to have a good time and mingle.

glosses.anímate: come on, go for it — informal command of animarse
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)
glosses.tienes: you have — 2nd person of tener (tienes que = you have to)
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.pasarla: to have a time (pasarla bien = to have a good time)
glosses.convivir: to spend time together, to mingle

note.en: Pasarla bien is a common phrase that means to have a good time. La refers to no noun in particular.
note.es: Pasarla bien significa divertirse. El pronombre la no se refiere a nada concreto; es una forma fija.

exercises.text: Me da gusto que hayas conseguido boletos para el concierto; yo quería ir, pero no encontré ninguno.
exercises.meaningEn: I am happy you got tickets for the concert; I wanted to go, but I could not find any.

glosses.da: gives (me da gusto = I am happy)
glosses.gusto: pleasure (me da gusto = I am glad)
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.hayas: (you) have — present subjunctive of haber, after me da gusto que
glosses.conseguido: gotten, obtained — past participle of conseguir
glosses.para: for, in order to (para que = so that, + subjunctive)

note.en: Me da gusto que takes the subjunctive. Ninguno keeps this form because no noun follows it.
note.es: Me da gusto que lleva subjuntivo. Ninguno se queda así porque no acompaña a un sustantivo.

exercises.text: Mi mamá dice que antes de que se acabe el domingo hay que descansar y llamar a los abuelos.
exercises.meaningEn: My mom says that before Sunday is over, you have to rest and call your grandparents.

glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.se: himself, itself; (le → se); se acabó = it ran out
glosses.acabe: (it) ends — present subjunctive of acabar, after antes de que
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)

note.en: Hay que plus infinitive means one must. It has no specific person as subject.
note.es: Hay que + infinitivo expresa una obligación general, sin decir quién la cumple.

exercises.text: Si me prestaras tu carro el sábado, te lo devolvería con el tanque lleno, de verdad.
exercises.meaningEn: If you lent me your car on Saturday, I would return it to you with a full tank, really.

exercises.text: Por si acaso hace frío en la noche, lleva una chamarra y avísame a qué hora regresas.
exercises.meaningEn: Just in case it gets cold at night, take a jacket and let me know what time you come back.

glosses.acaso: perhaps (por si acaso = just in case)
glosses.hace: makes, does (hace frío = it is cold)
glosses.lleva: takes, carries — 3rd person of llevar (lleva una chamarra = take a jacket)
glosses.avísame: let me know — command of avisar + me
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)
glosses.qué: what; how (qué bueno que = how good that)
glosses.regresas: you come back — 2nd person of regresar

note.en: Chamarra is the Mexican word for jacket. Avísame has a written accent because the stress falls on the third syllable from the end.
note.es: Chamarra es la palabra mexicana para chaqueta. Avísame lleva acento escrito por la regla de las palabras esdrújulas.

exercises.text: Se me hizo tarde y ya no alcancé el camión, pero mis amigos dijeron que me esperan.
exercises.meaningEn: I ran late and missed the bus, but my friends said they are waiting for me.

glosses.se: himself, itself; (le → se); se acabó = it ran out
glosses.hizo: (he) made, held — preterite of hacer (se me hizo tarde = I ran late)
glosses.alcancé: I caught, made it to — preterite of alcanzar
glosses.que: that, which; so that, who (after antecedent)
glosses.esperan: (they) wait for — 3rd person plural of esperar

note.en: Se me hizo tarde is the natural way to say I ran late. The event happens to me; I am not the cause.
note.es: Se me hizo tarde es la forma natural de decir llegué tarde: el hecho le pasó a uno, sin culpa.

exercises.text: Parra tenía una perra, Guerra tenía una parra. La perra de Parra subió a la parra de Guerra.
exercises.meaningEn: Parra had a dog, Guerra had a grapevine. Parra's dog climbed up Guerra's grapevine. (Tongue twister.)

glosses.parra: grapevine; also a surname in the tongue twister
glosses.guerra: war; here a surname in the tongue twister
glosses.a: to, at (also: personal a before people)

note.en: Trill the rr in Parra, perra, parra, and Guerra. Start slowly and speed up.
note.es: Trabalenguas tradicional. La rr es vibrante en parra, perra y guerra. Empieza despacio y ve acelerando.
